Unreachable difference under this engine's sort — a property of the implementation, not of stable sorting in general. The comparator's branches disagree only for two members with the same path, where the original answers 0 and the mutant answers 1; a stable sort that consumed the result as `> 0` anywhere would tell them apart — an insertion sort shifting on `compare(previous, current) > 0` reverses the pair under the mutant — so what makes the mutant unobservable is that no consumer of `Compare` tests `> 0`: in `deps/v8/third_party/v8/builtins/array-sort.tq` (V8 13.6.233.17 in Node v24.16.0, V8 14.1.146.11 in Node v25.9.0) insertion, run detection, both merge directions and both gallops all branch on `order < 0` or `order >= 0`, so 0 and 1 select the same transition at every site and the permutation is identical. A different engine, or a future V8 that tests `> 0`, would make the mutant observable. Measured corroboration on this engine: all-equal member lists at every length from 2 to 500, and about 400,000 randomised and run-built lists with equal paths split across merge boundaries, with no divergent permutation. Separately, and not part of the equivalence: since #215 a member list carrying one path twice is refused at admission on `bundle_inventory_duplicate`; the digest is still computed and returned for a refused candidate, so this narrows where a difference could matter rather than whether one can be observed. The sibling mutant on this line, `< -> <=`, answers -1 on equal paths, does reorder them under this same sort, and is killed by the pinned digests in 'a repeated member path refuses in either order'.

The two differ only when the separator is at position zero — a target directly under the filesystem root — where `'/'` and `''` both produce a resolved path outside any project root. The one root that would tell them apart is `/` itself, and the adapter now refuses that at construction (`fs_outside_project`), with a test. So no admitted project can reach an input where the branches disagree.

Unreachable difference under a stable sort. The comparator is `left < right ? -1 : left > right ? 1 : 0`, so its two remaining branches can only disagree on equal keys, where the original answers 0 and the mutant answers 1 — both meaning "do not move left before right". A stable sort never moves an element past one it does not compare strictly-before, so the permutation is identical: measured on runs of equal keys of length 2, 3, 4, 5, 10 and 15, and on mixed keys containing a duplicate, the original and the mutant agree on every one. The sibling mutant on this line, `< -> <=`, answers -1 on equal keys and does reorder them; it is killed by "two members a document should not have keep the order it wrote them in", so the line is covered and this is the single difference no input can show.

non_terminating_mutants.reason: `while (queue.length > 0)` is the only exit of `impactClosure`. `> -> >=` makes an empty queue (`length === 0`) still enter the body. `queue.shift()` then yields `undefined`; `byName.get(undefined)?.impacts ?? []` is empty, so nothing is enqueued and the condition stays true. `seen` only suppresses re-enqueue of a named class — it is not the loop condition — so even a cycle-free registry hangs once the work list drains. The mutant never returns an impact set.

`while (ready.length > 0)` is Kahn termination in `kahnOrder`: empty `ready` means the remaining nodes are a cycle (or the graph is done). `> -> >=` keeps that empty list in the body. `ready.shift()` yields `undefined`, which is pushed onto `order` every iteration; `children.get(undefined) ?? []` adds nothing back. The mutant never returns, so `graphErrors` cannot observe `order.length !== tickets.length` and the cycle refusal is unreachable.

`while (stack.length > 0)` is the only way `reaches` inside `comparable` returns false. `> -> >=` keeps an empty stack in the body. `stack.pop()` yields `undefined`; `byId.get(undefined)?.depends_on ?? []` is empty, so the `parent === to` hit and the `stack.push` never run, and `return false` after the loop is unreachable. `seen` only skips parents already walked — it does not stop the loop — so a fully explored (even acyclic) walk hangs instead of answering.

`demand(!seen.has(receipt.staging_commit_oid), 'containment_mismatch', …)` is the only break of a receipt cycle in `lineageFor`. Neutralising it leaves `while (cursor !== head)` walking `cursor = receipt.staging_commit_oid`. On a loop (a→b, b→a) every cursor is a key in `byBase`, so `if (!receipt) break` never fires, and `head` off the cycle (the existing test uses `z`) is never reached. `seen.add` of a repeat is a no-op and is not a loop condition. The test that feeds that loop is correct — it asserts `containment_mismatch` — but without the demand the walk does not return a value to assert.
